title: Modular Power Tower a^(b^c) mod P
description: Given non-negative 64-bit integers `a`, `b`, `c` and a prime modulus `p`, compute the power tower `a^(b^c) % p` (evaluated right-associatively as `a` raised to the power `(b^c)`). Follow the convention `0^0 = 1`.
constraints: p is guaranteed to be a prime number.
hints: Handle the zero-exponent case `b^c == 0` first (which happens if and only if `b == 0` and `c > 0`, yielding `a^0 % p = 1`); otherwise `b^c >= 1`, so if `a % p == 0`, the answer is `0`.
When `a % p != 0`, Fermat's Little Theorem gives `a^(p - 1) == 1 (mod p)`, so reduce the exponent `e = b^c mod (p - 1)` with binary exponentiation and then return `a^e mod p`.
